title: Add ingress fairness quota and fast‑lane admission to stop mixed‑workload long‑context cascades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Urgent customer escalation: observed repeated long-tail latency spikes in Dedicated and Hosted clusters when large enterprise tenant submits mixed traffic (high-rate short chats + intermittent multi-thousand-token offline jobs). Investigation points to admission imbalance and KV-cache thrashing causing queue starvation for short flows. This ticket designs, implements, and rolls out a granular per-ingress fairness quota and a transient 'fast-lane' admission path for short/latency-sensitive requests to prevent cascades during mixed-workload waves.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a mixed workload: 80% short chat requests (<= 64 tokens, QPS 1200) + 20% long offline requests (>= 4k tokens, bursty every 30s) against a Dedicated pool with continuous batching enabled.
2) Observe scheduler admission windows and KV cache churn metrics for the affected host.
3) Notice short-request P99 latency degrade and queue length growth correlating with long-request admission windows.
4) Reproduce in a Private deployment under rolling upgrade scenario where admission bookkeeping briefly desynchronizes.
root_cause: The continuous batching admission window and prefetch subsystem prioritizes filling GPU batches (to maximize throughput) with minimal awareness of request latency sensitivity. Long-context requests cause KV-cache hotness and eviction cycles; the admission reservoir is ephemeral and can be consumed by a few long requests, starving short, latency-sensitive flows. Additionally, during upgrades/maintenance windows the admission state was not correctly reconciled, amplifying starvation.
mitigation: Applied an emergency throttle on long-request admission for impacted tenants (hotfix deployed 2026-02-22) and enabled temporary admission quotas per-tenant to preserve short-request throughput. Also surfaced dedicated dashboard with 'fast-lane hit rate' and KV-cache eviction indicators for customers and SREs.
proposed_solution:
1) Implement per-ingress granular fairness quotas that maintain a minimum admission share for latency-sensitive classes (short, interactive) even under high long-request pressure.
2) Add a 'fast-lane' admission path: ephemeral admission tokens reserved for requests tagged short/interactive; tokens refill proportionally to short-request QPS and decay quickly to avoid long-request starvation.
3) Integrate KV-cache hotness signals into admission (if eviction rate > threshold, reduce long-request admission and raise fast-lane token refill temporarily).
4) Add reconciliation logic for upgrade/maintenance windows to avoid admission state divergence across hosts and make it eventual-consistent with conservative defaults on startup.
architecture_decisions:
- Use existing tenant-level admission bookkeeping; add delta fields to track 'fast-lane' balance.
- Keep admission changes as runtime-configurable flags behind feature-flag to canary rollout.
- Use telemetry-derived thresholds initially; plan for ML-derived adaptive thresholds in follow-up.
- Avoid per-request synchronous KV cache checks; rely on aggregated host-level eviction signals to make admission decisions.
implementation_notes:
- New components: fast_lane_manager (ephemeral token bucket), quota_enforcer (per-ingress min-share), eviction_watcher (aggregates KV eviction rates).
- Modify scheduler admission path to consult fast_lane_manager for requests with attribute 'latency_class: short'.
- Add admin API to adjust per-tenant min_share and fast-lane refill intervals for Dedicated customers.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged canary on internal staging clusters (2 hosts) — 2 days.
2) Canary on non-production customer Dedicated pool with observability hooks — 3 days.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% of Dedicated capacity + all Hosted routes with low-traffic customers — 1 week.
4) Full rollout after 2 weeks with retention of metrics and automatic rollback conditions (P99 short-request latency > baseline * 1.5 or KV-eviction spike).
qa_plan:
- Synthetic mixed-workload tests with deterministic generators (short/long mixes) and chaos injection to simulate upgrade windows.
- End-to-end perf tests measuring P50/P95/P99 for short and long requests, KV-cache eviction rates, batch fill efficiency.
- Backwards compatibility checks: ensure no regressions for single-workload deployments.
- Integration tests for Private/VPC upgrade scenario reconcilers.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket opened after urgent customer PM escalated production incidents (INC-2026-00432). Initial triage assigned to on-call SRE and scheduler team.

2026-02-22: Hotfix throttles long-request admission for the affected tenant; immediate P99 short-request latency improved from ~820ms to ~140ms. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/15987

2026-02-25: Root cause confirmed via deterministic replay and KV eviction correlation graphs (dashboard link below). Decision made to build a fast-lane token system rather than hard static quotas to preserve throughput economics.

2026-03-01: Fast-lane manager prototype merged to internal feature branch; unit tests and initial integration tests green. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321
2026-03-04: Canary rollout started on 2 non-prod Dedicated hosts; early telemetry shows 60% reduction in short-request tail events without significant throughput loss for long jobs.
2026-03-07: Addressed edge case where fast-lane tokens failed to refill after host restart (fix in PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/16033). Preparing wider canary next week.
Next: Expand canary, run private upgrade reconcilers, finalize runbook and SLO guardrails before full rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fast-lane could reduce GPU utilization if refill rates are too aggressive. Mitigation: conservative default refill and telemetry-backed autoscale of refill based on utilization windows.

Risk: Complexity in per-tenant quotas increases operational overhead. Mitigation: provide sane defaults and an admin UI for quick adjustments; default only enabled for tenants with observed mixed workloads.

Risk: Feature-flag divergence between hosts during private upgrades. Mitigation: implement reconciliation that enforces conservative admission on boot until feature flag state confirmed by control-plane.

Risk: Potential attack surface if clients mark all requests as 'short'. Mitigation: require router/client SDKs to sign request attribute; validate token sizes server-side and impose 'short' eligibility checks (<= 128 tokens) at the edge.
Risk: Regression to long-request throughput SLA. Mitigation: rollout gates with throughput and cost guardrails; adjustable long-request backpressure knobs per customer tier.
notes: Customer SME: contacted at 2026-02-20 16:12 PST; provided mitigation notes and will participate in canary review.
Follow-up: evaluate applying adaptive refill rate based on observed short-request percent and host GPU utilization (phase 2).
Observability: add 'fast_lane_take_rate' and 'fast_lane_refill_rate' to per-host telemetry with 1s granularity.
